points: Q3 will reveal whether Fitness's 25% Q2 growth carried into late summer, and whether demand for advanced wearables plus the new CIRQA Smart Band is adding incremental revenue ahead of the holiday build.
The print will test whether Q2's gross margin of 62.4% and operating margin of 30.4% are durable; holding or expanding those levels would confirm the margin-leverage case behind the long.

After Garmin raised full-year guidance in Q2, the Q3 report will show if management is confident enough to maintain or lift that guidance again, which matters for the 18% FY1 EPS growth path and the 7-up/0-down revision trend.

Aviation and Marine grew 8% and 14% in Q2, and the new AXIS flight-display family should keep those higher-margin segments supportive through Q3 and into Q4, helping offset any lingering Outdoor weakness.
Outdoor revenue fell 2% in Q2; Q3 results and commentary will show whether adventure watches and consumer auto remain a drag or stabilize, which shapes Q4 holiday positioning.

The Q4 and FY2 setup depends on new product ramps and the TrainingPeaks/TrainHeroic integration contributing to revenue and services mix; Q3 commentary on sell-through and integration progress will shape the 8.7% FY2 EPS growth case.
watch: Fitness segment revenue growth stays strong relative to Q2's 25% pace — supports the long.
Consolidated gross margin holds at or above Q2's 62.4% — supports the long.
Full-year EPS guidance is maintained or raised after the Q2 increase — supports the long.
Aviation plus Marine revenue growth remains positive and offsets any Outdoor softness — supports the long.
